titulo: The simple future: Predictions, promises and probability

aula.objetivo: Form the simple future of regular verbs (infinitive + endings) and of the ten most common irregular ones (tendré, haré, diré, podré, pondré, saldré, vendré, sabré, querré, habré), use it for plans, predictions, and promises, and recognize the time markers that go with it.

blocos.titulo: What the future is for: predictions, promises, and guesses
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: prediction: the future describes what's expected to happen. «Mañana lloverá en el norte», «La semana que viene hará más frío». STEP 2: promise and firm decision: «Te lo prometo: estudiaré todos los días», «Mañana te llamaré». STEP 3: a soft command with a note of authority: «Mañana vendrás a las nueve», which isn't a question but a heads-up that barely leaves room to say no. Use it carefully. STEP 4: doubt or guessing about the present: «¿Dónde estará Ana?» (I wonder where Ana is) and «Estará en casa» (She must be home). This only works with the simple future. English actually does something similar with "will": "She'll be home by now" works as a guess about the present the same way «Estará en casa» does — so this particular use transfers more naturally than most of this lesson. STEP 5: use time markers to place the action: «mañana», «el año que viene», «dentro de una semana». «Dentro de» means "in," the same "in" as English "in an hour": «Llegaré dentro de una hora» is "I'll arrive in an hour." STEP 6: «en una hora» can also mean the same thing, but «dentro de» is the clearer choice. STEP 7: with «cuando» and the future, Spanish uses the present (subjunctive) in the «cuando» clause: «Cuando llegues, te llamaré» — you'll see why later; for now just learn the pattern as a fixed phrase. STEP 8: weather talk: «llover» (llueve, lloverá), «hacer sol / calor / frío / viento», «estar nublado».
blocos.comparacao: English predictions use "it's going to rain" or "it will rain" about as interchangeably as Spanish uses «va a llover» and «lloverá», so that part feels familiar. The real overlap worth noticing is the guessing use: English "he'll be tired" or "that'll be John" works the same way as «estará cansado» — both languages reach for the future tense to mark a confident guess, not just something scheduled to happen.

tabela.traducao: [misto] It will rain in Galicia tomorrow.

tabela.exemplo: [misto] El año que viene estudiaré inglés.
tabela.traducao: [misto] Next year I'm going to study English.

erros.motivo: The impersonal «haber» stays singular, even with a plural.

erros.errado: [misto] Estará muy cansado. (meaning "he's tired, I'm sure")
erros.motivo: The future of guessing signals doubt; for a plain fact, use the present.

blocos.titulo: El tiempo de la semana / The week's weather
blocos.ru: La semana que viene habrá mucho cambio. El lunes hará sol y la temperatura subirá hasta veinte grados. El martes se nublará por la tarde y el miércoles lloverá en el norte. El jueves hará mucho viento, pero el viernes saldrá el sol otra vez. Marta tiene planes para el fin de semana: si hace buen tiempo, saldrá a pasear con su hermano y comerán en el campo. Si llueve, se quedarán en casa y verán una película.
blocos.pt: Next week will bring a lot of change. On Monday it'll be sunny and the temperature will climb to twenty degrees. On Tuesday it'll get cloudy in the afternoon, and on Wednesday it'll rain in the north. On Thursday it'll be very windy, but on Friday the sun will come out again. Marta has plans for the weekend: if the weather's good, she'll go out for a walk with her brother and they'll have lunch in the countryside. If it rains, they'll stay home and watch a movie.

perguntas.pergunta: [misto] ¿Qué hará Marta si hace buen tiempo?
perguntas.resposta: [misto] Saldrá a pasear con su hermano.
[misto] Se quedarán en casa y verán una película.

blocos.enunciado: Give the weather forecast for your city for the next three days, out loud, using the future. Then say what you'll do if it rains.
Say from memory the ten irregular futures in the «yo» form. Make a sentence with each of the first four.
